family.name: Hummer H1
family.verdict: An Army truck with carpets, built on the same line as the real thing and twice as wide as common sense. It goes almost anywhere, seats four, and asks for an idler arm in return.
intro: In 1983 AM General won the Army contract for the M998 High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle, the HMMWV, and it had already trademarked the nickname its prototypes went by: Hummer. After the Gulf War made the truck famous, and with Arnold Schwarzenegger lobbying for a road-legal version, AM General began selling a civilian Hummer in 1992. It was built in Mishawaka, Indiana, alongside the military trucks.

The [[hummer/h1|Hummer H1]] kept the hardware that matters off-road: geared portal hubs, inboard disc brakes, a central tire inflation system and 16 inches of ground clearance. GM diesels powered most of them, from the 6.2 to the 6.5 turbo, plus a 5.7 gas V8 for two years and the Duramax in the final 2006 Alpha. AM General built 11,818 of them, ending in June 2006.

GM bought the Hummer brand in 1999. It renamed the original truck the H1 and added its own H2 and H3, both built on GM truck platforms, before closing the brand in 2010. GM revived the name in 2020 for the electric GMC Hummer EV. Only the H1 is a HMMWV underneath, and it's the only one this site covers.

page.title: Hummer H1
page.eyebrow: AM GENERAL HUMMER H1 · CIVILIAN HMMWV · 1992–2006
page.verdict: A military truck with a stereo, built on the same line as the Army's and engineered to follow tanks. It's slow and wide, and it eats front ends, but geared hubs, inboard brakes and CTIS let it go places nothing else this size can.

paragraphs: The Hummer H1 is what happened when a defense contractor took a call from a movie star. Underneath, it's the Army's M998 HMMWV with gloss paint, carpet and a stereo. The frame, axles and brakes are shared with the military trucks, and so are the hood, tailgate and quarter panels. AM General built both versions on the same Mishawaka, Indiana, line from 1992 to 2006, 11,818 civilian trucks in all. It is 86.5 inches wide, seats four either side of a driveline tunnel the size of a footlocker, and can climb a 22-inch step. Nothing else on this site was built to that brief.

story.heading: FROM JEEP'S DEFENSE ARM TO THE HUMVEE
paragraphs: AM General began as the General Products Division of Kaiser Jeep, the old Studebaker defense plant in South Bend. American Motors made it a subsidiary in 1971. In 1979 the Army published draft specifications for one truck to replace the M151 jeep, the M561 Gama Goat and the commercial-based CUCV pickups. It had to have a diesel, 16 inches of ground clearance and enough ability to climb a 60 percent grade. AM General developed its entry as a private venture and finished its first prototype in August 1980.

In July 1981 the Army ordered 11 prototypes each from AM General, Chrysler and Teledyne. They were tested at Aberdeen Proving Ground and Yuma. On March 22, 1983, AM General won the production contract for 55,000 HMMWVs. That same year LTV bought AM General: Renault had taken a large stake in AMC, and federal rules barred defense contractors owned by foreign governments, which included partly state-owned Renault. AM General had nicknamed its prototypes 'Hummer' and had the foresight to trademark it. Humvees were in service by 1985.

story.heading: ARNOLD'S TRUCK
paragraphs: AM General had considered a civilian model since the late 1980s. Gulf War photographs and Arnold Schwarzenegger, who saw an Army convoy while filming Kindergarten Cop in Oregon, made the case. The civilian Hummer went on sale in 1992, and Schwarzenegger bought the first two. At first there were no dealers. You ordered from the factory and could collect the truck in Indiana. Flash Off-Road's year-by-year guide lists the 1992 truck with a mechanical 150-hp 6.2-liter GM diesel, a three-speed 3L80 automatic and a 65-mph top speed. It built 316 that year.

Then came constant change. Because of how the military contracts were written, AM General slipped fixes into production as soon as they were ready, not just at model-year changes. In 1994 the trucks got the 6.5 diesel and a four-speed 4L80-E. For 1995 a 5.7-liter gas V8 was offered to buyers who were wary of diesel, and it was dropped during 1996. In 1996 the 6.5 turbo diesel and a second fuel tank arrived, and by 1997 the turbo made 195 hp and 430 lb-ft.

story.heading: HOW IT CLEARS 16 INCHES
paragraphs: The H1's clearance doesn't come from a lift. Each wheel has a geared hub, a portal reduction box with a 1.92:1 ratio in the 1999 brochure. It sits the axle shaft above the wheel center, so the halfshafts and differentials ride high in a channel down the middle of the truck. The disc brakes are inboard, next to the differentials, rather than in the wheels. Suspension is independent double A-arms with coil springs at every corner, and the track is 71.6 inches, wide enough to follow tank tracks. Mercedes used the same portal-axle trick decades later on the [[g-class/4x4-squared|G 500 4×4²]].

Wading depth is 30 inches with a diesel, thanks to a high air intake and a radiator mounted high and sloped over the engine. The central tire inflation system lets the driver air the tires down or up from the cab, front and rear pairs together, and runflat inserts were optional. Torsen I differentials handled traction through 1998. In 1999 ABS arrived, along with Torsen II units and electronic TorqTrac4 traction control, and Eaton electric lockers followed from 2003.

story.heading: GM, THE ALPHA AND THE END
paragraphs: In December 1999 General Motors bought the Hummer brand name and took over marketing. AM General kept building the truck, now called the H1, and also built GM's own H2 under contract. GM's smaller H3 came from a GM plant in Shreveport, Louisiana. In 2001 AM General began building the 6.5 diesels itself, having taken over GM's engine plant, and the 2004 'Optimizer' 6.5 made 205 hp. That set up the last and best H1: the Alpha, shown in Anaheim on October 27, 2004.

The Alpha used GM's 6.6-liter Duramax LLY, rated at 300 hp and 520 lb-ft, with an Allison five-speed automatic. To make room, AM General lifted the body 2 inches and redesigned the cooling. It also fitted helical-cut gears in the hubs, a stronger steering box and 51 gallons of fuel. There was no 2005 model year. Only 729 Alphas were built, at about $128,000 to $140,000 each. In May 2006 GM announced the end, with sales slow and new diesel emissions rules due for 2007, and production stopped in June. The Hummer brand itself closed in 2010. The name returned in 2020 on the electric GMC Hummer EV.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · BODY STYLES
callout.title: Wagon, open top, pickup, slant-back
paragraphs: AM General's VIN chart lists a two-door pickup, a four-door pickup, the station wagon and an open-body soft top, plus fleet and 'Recruit' versions. For 1995 it added an extended-cab two-door truck and an open top with full hard doors. The wagon got barn doors instead of a tailgate that year. The two-door short-cab pickup and the half-door open top were dropped for 1997, and the two- and four-door hardtops were dropped after 2001 except for fleet buyers.

In 2000 the factory offered a slant-back with the same body shape as the military Humvee. Flash Off-Road counts just 39 built, which makes it the rarest regular H1. By the end, individual buyers could only choose the soft-top open top or the wagon, and those were the only two bodies offered on the 2006 Alpha.

page.engineering_intro: The H1 is the HMMWV's driveline under a civilian body. A steel ladder frame carries independent double-A-arm suspension at all four corners. The engine sits well back, and the transmission, transfer case and both differentials run down a central tunnel. Halfshafts from the differentials drive geared hubs at the wheels, which drop the wheel center below the axle line. That's where the 16 inches of clearance comes from, along with the inboard brakes mounted at the differentials.

engineering.note: 1.92:1 (1999). Spur gears, cross-cut for noise from 1999; helical on the Alpha
10.5-in rotors at the differentials; ABS from 1999; 12-in rotors on the Alpha
Torsen I to 1998, Torsen II with TorqTrac4 from 1999; Eaton E-lockers from 2003
Inflate or deflate front and rear pairs from the cab; runflat inserts optional

buying_checks.head: Cold-start the turbo diesel and check the coolant
buying_checks.body: 1996 to early-1999 6.5 turbo diesels can crack at the No. 8 cylinder. Flash Off-Road's test: with the engine stone cold, open the radiator cap, run the engine for about a minute, shut it off and open the cap again. Pressure in the coolant, foaming at the bleeder once it's warm, or milky sludge in the CDR valve point to a cracked block or head gasket. A 'Z' in the fourth VIN digit is a GM-built turbo engine; an 'F' is the later AM General engine.

buying_checks.head: Front-end play
buying_checks.body: Flash Off-Road calls the front end the H1's biggest weakness: idler arms, pitman arms and steering gears wear out. With the engine running, if the steering wheel moves an inch or two before the front wheels do, suspect the pitman arm. If the steering turns more easily one way than the other, suspect the steering box. Uneven tire wear points to worn front-end parts or a bad alignment.

buying_checks.head: Geared-hub and halfshaft leaks
buying_checks.body: A fan of oil sprayed on the inside of a tire means a leaking hub seal. So does a CTIS that won't hold air, through the spindle seal. Look for torn halfshaft boots, and wet spots where the shafts meet the differentials and hubs. Wet calipers can be differential oil, because the brakes sit right next to the differentials.

buying_checks.head: Make the CTIS work
buying_checks.body: Run the pump on the fronts, the rears and all four, and watch the cab gauge. Owners do abandon CTIS when the pump dies, and Flash Off-Road says a new pump can cost well over $1,000. Retrofitting CTIS, the four-speed transmission or the second fuel tank to a truck that lacks them is hard and rarely worth it, so buy the features you want.

buying_checks.head: Transfer case fluid and the 'vampire'
buying_checks.body: Pull the transfer case fill plug. If fluid pours out, the cooler loop inside the case may be leaking transmission fluid into it, the 'vampire' that AM General addressed with customer-satisfaction campaign R0101 in 2001. Brown, burnt fluid is a sign of long stretches at 80 mph. Flash Off-Road recommends keeping it under about 65 mph (2,400 rpm).

buying_checks.head: Heater and A/C: pre- or post-1997.5
buying_checks.body: The HVAC system used from 1994 leaked heater cores and was replaced from VIN 176477 (the '97.5'). Flash Off-Road says the old parts are discontinued and the upgrade runs $3,000 to $4,000. Upgraded systems use a vacuum-controlled heater valve and lack separate recirculate and A/C buttons on the control head.

buying_checks.head: Correct wheels and tires
buying_checks.body: Every H1 wheel uses an 8x6.5-in bolt pattern with a 7-in backset. Flash Off-Road says only AM General and GT/Cepek wheels have the right offset and load rating. Wrong wheels stress the front end, need custom CTIS lines and throw dirt up the sides. Tires for 16.5-in wheels are scarce, so check the spare.

buying_checks.head: Body, rockers and underside
buying_checks.body: The body is aluminum but the doors and wagon top are steel. Expect some corrosion where the two meet and around the marker lights, and lift the wheel-well carpet on wagons to check the inner seams. Look for bent rockers and undercarriage protection pushed up against the exhaust, which comes from off-road use.

repairs.title: Replace geared-hub output and spindle seals
repairs.symptoms: Oil sprayed on the inside of a tire, oil dripping off the lower ball joint, or a CTIS pair that loses pressure overnight. Pull the hub's breather line and put it under water: bubbles mean CTIS air is leaking past the spindle seal into the hub.
repairs.fix: Jack under the lower A-arm and chock the truck. Disconnect the CTIS line on the opposite wheel so it doesn't deflate. Drain the hub with a 5/16-in hex. Remove the CTIS line and the four 3/4-in steering-arm cover bolts, then the snap ring, and tap out the small spindle seal. Remove the clamp-nut lock screw and the clamp nut, and lay out the nut, keyed washer and bearing in order. Pull the spindle, drive out the output seal, clean the bore and the spindle's sealing surface, and drive the new seal flat. Reassemble following the AM General manual's clamp-nut sequence with red Loctite 272 inside its 10-minute window (lock screw 90 lb-in). Clear the hub vent line, then refill with GL-5 80W-90 or 75W-90 to just under the fill plug, about half a quart.
repairs.tools: 5/16-in hex · 5/8 and 13/16-in wrenches · 3/4-in socket · 5/32-in hex socket · clamp-nut socket (Flash Off-Road made one from a NAPA 2467 Dana 44 spindle socket) · snap-ring pliers · inch-lb and ft-lb torque wrenches · Loctite 272 and 518 · output seal 5579060, spindle seal 6005193 (Flash Off-Road)

parts.name: H1 Geared Hub Heat Sink (billet access covers, set of 4)
Heavy-duty billet aluminum geared hub kit, 1992–2006 H1

repairs.title: Replace the idler and pitman arms
repairs.symptoms: Steering wheel off-center or loose, with an inch or more of free play before the wheels move. Front tires that splay apart over obstacles. A shimmy at around 35 mph that fades by 40. The shop manual's limits are 5/16 in of vertical play at the center link for the idler, 1/8 in for the pitman, and 1/32 in at either ball stud.
repairs.fix: Unbolt the idler arm from the frame and separate it from the center link with a puller or pickle fork. Flash Off-Road had to cut away the rubber seal first. With the idler off, the center link drops and the pitman arm comes off the steering box shaft. Pack grease around the box output shaft. Fit the new pitman on the splines and the center link together, torque the big nut to 180 lb-ft and the 15/16-in ball-stud nut to 80 lb-ft, and line up the cotter pin. Bolt the new idler to the frame at 60 lb-ft and its ball stud at 80 lb-ft, then grease both. 1993–94 trucks with the 7/8-in center link need spacers; the 1-in link started at VIN 163985.
repairs.tools: Pitman puller · 1-5/16-in socket and breaker bar · 18 mm, 11/16 and 5/8-in sockets · torque wrench to 180 lb-ft · jack stands · cotter pins · AM General idler 5745558 and pitman 6011300 (Flash Off-Road, 2005)

repairs.title: Relocate the 6.5 TD's pump-mounted driver (PMD/FSD)
repairs.symptoms: A turbo diesel that stalls when hot and restarts once it cools, then gets harder to restart as the fault worsens. Codes P0251 and P0370 point at the injection pump's optical sensor and the PMD. A fuel shutoff solenoid problem is different: it sputters before stalling.
repairs.fix: First rule out fuel: change the filter, check the lift pump and look for a kinked return hose. The Stanadyne DS4831 pump on 1996–2004 turbo diesels carries its electronic driver (PMD, also called FSD) on the pump itself, in the engine's heat. Fit a new PMD on a remote heat sink outside the engine bay, with thermal paste and the extension harness. If codes persist, have a Stanadyne shop check the pump; Flash Off-Road says to fit a DS4831-5288 or -5521, not the early -5067.
repairs.tools: Torx and socket set · thermal compound · scan tool to read and clear codes · Stanadyne fuel additive

parts.name: Fuel pump drive module (PMD), 1998 H1 6.5 TD (catalog)
H1 RapCool High Performance PMD Isolator

repairs.title: Replace the fuel shutoff solenoid
repairs.cost: Parts only (about $70 rebuilt in 2012, per Flash Off-Road)
repairs.symptoms: Occasional hard starts, sputtering and stalling while driving, and an engine that won't restart straight away. This differs from a PMD fault, which usually stalls without sputtering.
repairs.fix: Disconnect the connector and unscrew the solenoid from the top of the injection pump (1/2-in hex). Don't lose the coil spring in the bore, and keep dirt out of the pump. Install the new solenoid, torque it to 200 lb-in per Stanadyne, and reconnect it.
repairs.tools: 1/2-in wrench · inch-lb torque wrench · clean rags

repairs.title: Find and fix a CTIS leak
repairs.time: ≈ An afternoon to several days of testing
repairs.symptoms: One axle's tires drop pressure overnight, or CTIS won't inflate or deflate at all. The fronts and rears are paired, so a leak can be in either tire, either hub seal, the lines, the manifold solenoids, the over-pressure valve or the pump.
repairs.fix: Spray soapy water on the tires, rims, lines and fittings. Inflate to normal, pull both quick-disconnects at the wheels and leave it overnight. If the cab gauge drops, the leak is in the lines, manifold or pump; if not, reconnect one wheel at a time to find the leaking tire or hub. Bubble-test each hub vent for a bad spindle seal. Check the braided hose swivel at the hub with the wheels turned both ways. Clean sand out of the manifold solenoid valves. If the pump won't run, jump it from the battery, then check the 5-amp (1G) and 40-amp fuses and the relay, per Gil Herman's checklist on Flash Off-Road.
repairs.tools: Spray bottle · 7/8-in and 1-3/16-in deep sockets (the latter sold as a GM oil-sender socket) · 9/16-in wrench · multimeter · jumper lead

parts.name: Stainless Steel Inboard CTIS Lines – full kit

repairs.title: Rebuild or replace a halfshaft
repairs.cost: Boot kits under $10 locally in Flash Off-Road's report; a shop charged $25 a boot or $50 a joint
repairs.symptoms: Torn boots throwing grease, clicking on turns, or a worn seal surface where the shaft enters the hub input seal.
repairs.fix: The halfshaft bolts to the inboard brake rotor at one end and splines into the geared hub at the other. On the right rear you must remove the parking brake cable to get it out. Each CV joint has a star, cage and six balls, and the cage is usually what fails. Flash Off-Road says the 1994-on joints share Rockford parts with the 1993–98 Mercury Villager and Ford Explorer. Fit new boots and clips, and a Speedi-Sleeve (99199) if the seal surface is grooved. Reinstall the six M10 class 10.9 bolts with new Nord-Lock washer pairs and red Loctite at 57 lb-ft. Overtightening can warp the rotor.
repairs.tools: 3/8-in drive short socket and extension · retaining-ring pliers · CV boot crimper · torque wrench · Nord-Lock washers · Loctite 272

parts.name: H1 Heavy Duty 12k Half Shaft Kit

repairs.title: Replace inboard brake pads (and rotors)
repairs.symptoms: Pads under 1/8 in, chatter from new pads, a pulsing pedal from warped rotors, or fluid on the caliper from a piston seal.
repairs.fix: The front and rear pads are the same; the front calipers are Jeep parts and the rears carry the parking brake. Fronts retract with pliers, while the rear pistons must be turned to retract. Flash Off-Road shows how to do it without the $350 Kent-Moore tool. Chamfer the edges of new pads to stop chatter. Rotors have a minimum thickness of 0.815 in cast into them. Replacing or turning them means removing the halfshaft bolts, so have new Nord-Lock washers ready.
repairs.tools: Channel-lock pliers · piston tool for the rears · 3/8-in flare-nut wrench (1/2-in for the caliper fitting) · brake fluid (DOT 5 silicone to 1998, DOT 3 from 1999) · AM General pad 5745162C (Flash Off-Road)

parts.name: High Performance Semi Metallic Brake Pads

repairs.title: Test and replace glow plugs
repairs.cost: Plugs about $10–12 each in Flash Off-Road's report
repairs.symptoms: Hard cold starts that get worse as temperatures drop, or black smoke and a stall right after starting. Flash Off-Road's 1996 turbo diesel wouldn't start below 50°F when its plugs failed.
repairs.fix: With the ignition on, the voltmeter should dip as the plugs draw current. Measure about 50–55 amps per bank and 13–14 amps per plug while they cycle (6.5 non-turbo procedure; military 24-volt trucks are different). Replace failed plugs; Flash Off-Road recommends the self-limiting AC 60G. Check the controller and alternator voltage too, because both can burn out plugs. They aren't a routine service item.
repairs.tools: Multimeter with a DC amp clamp or in-line ammeter · deep sockets · anti-seize

baseline_service.intro: Assume the last owner skipped things. H1s changed constantly in production, so decode the VIN first: the fourth digit is the engine and the fifth the transmission. AM General's HUMMER Recommended Maintenance Schedule (#0574480) runs on a 3,000-mile cycle with inspection groups A, B and C, and a truck that's over 24,000 miles and behind on service should start at the 12,000-mile service.

items.spec: Diesel-rated oil (Flash Off-Road uses Shell Rotella T) · 6.5 TD ≈ 7.5 qt, 6.5 NA ≈ 8 qt with filter
items.interval: Every 3,000 mi on the factory schedule
items.note: Flash Off-Road uses a Delco PF-1218 filter. Diesel oil turns black almost at once, which is normal.
Don't forget the two steering-column fittings behind the kick panel and the one in the steering shaft U-joint under the hood. Go easy on the front driveshaft slip joint or you'll pop the cap.

items.spec: Replace element; drain water from the filter bowl
items.interval: Element every 6,000 mi on the factory schedule; drain as needed
items.note: Water reaching the injectors destroys them. Carry a spare filter off-road.
Flash Off-Road advises against K&N filters on H1s. The geared hubs and transfer case vent into the air cleaner, so keep the housing sealed.

items.spec: Coolant type [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] · ≈25 L (26 US qt) system on the 6.5 diesels (Liqui Moly lookup) · two 195°F thermostats, GM 12559336
items.interval: Flush every 12,000 mi on the factory schedule
items.note: Flash Off-Road weighs nitrite-protected diesel coolants such as Fleet Charge against regular antifreeze; its author went back to regular antifreeze, citing the 6.5's thick, unsleeved cylinder walls. It also reports a batch of bad thermostats in the supply chain around 2000. On a turbo diesel, run the No. 8 cylinder pressure check at the same time.

items.spec: Dexron III per Flash Off-Road · Allison 1000 fluid on the Alpha [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.interval: Service every 12,000 mi on the factory schedule
items.note: There are three different filter and pickup designs depending on the year and pan depth, so match the filter. Flash Off-Road flushes every 35,000 mi or so and changes the filter after 50,000.

items.spec: Dexron III; Flash Off-Road recommends synthetic Dexron
items.interval: Service every 12,000 mi on the factory schedule
items.note: If it's overfull or pours out when you open the fill plug, the cooler loop is leaking ('the vampire', AM General campaign R0101).

items.spec: GL-5 gear oil · trucks with Eaton E-lockers need AM General synthetic 75W-90 with friction modifier · ≈1.9 L (2.0 US qt) per differential on the 6.5 diesels (Liqui Moly lookup)
items.interval: Check level and condition at every Group A inspection
items.note: Tags on the covers give the ratio and Torsen type. 1998 and later trucks use 2.56:1, earlier ones 2.73:1.

items.spec: GL-5 80W-90 or 75W-90 · about 1/2 qt per hub
items.interval: Check at every Group A inspection; change after deep water
items.note: Milky oil means water got in through a seal or a cracked vent line. Drain and fill plugs need only 8–13 lb-ft.

items.spec: DOT 5 silicone on 1992–1998 trucks; DOT 3 on 1999-on trucks with ABS (Flash Off-Road)
items.interval: Flush at purchase, then per the manual
items.note: Never mix the two: silicone DOT 5 and glycol DOT 3 don't blend, and Flash Off-Road says two colors in the reservoir mean someone has. The 1999–2000 trucks had a recall for chafing master-cylinder-to-ABS lines. Check the brake lines for corrosion.

items.spec: Idler arm, pitman arm, tie rods, ball joints
items.interval: Inspect every 3,000 mi; alignment check every 12,000
items.note: Flash Off-Road says aligning a pre-'97.5 truck means shimming the upper A-arms and can take 6–8 hours; eccentric washers made camber adjustable from 1998.

items.interval: Inspect bolts every 3,000 mi and boots every 6,000 mi
items.note: The factory figure was originally 48 lb-ft; Flash Off-Road gives 57 lb-ft as the current recommendation.

items.spec: Inflate and deflate test, front, rear and both
items.note: Flash Off-Road suggests 30–37 psi cold on the road, depending on the tire.

parts.name: Stainless Steel Inboard CTIS Lines – full kit

items.spec: Inspect the belt; check battery voltage and condition
items.interval: Belt every 6,000 mi; batteries checked at 24,000 mi
items.note: Batteries moved under the hood in 1994; 1992–93 trucks keep them under the passenger seat.

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: The factory tire was a 37x12.50R16.5, and later trucks used 37-inch tires on 17-inch wheels. Flash Off-Road says a 38x15.5 is the largest you can run on stock wheels without lifting the truck, though you need to watch for rubbing on the suspension at full lock. Taller tires need a body lift: Flash Off-Road reports owners running 39.5s with a 2-inch body lift and no rubbing.

Flash Off-Road says many owners consider the 1998 the quintessential pre-Alpha truck. It has the 1997.5 HVAC, better sound insulation, the 2.56 axles and the last of the Torsen I differentials, before ABS and TorqTrac4 arrived in 1999. Its turbo diesel sits right in the No. 8 crack window, though (see the next question), so test the block or look for a replacement engine. Flash Off-Road calls the 2004, with its new interior, Optimizer engine and optional Eaton lockers, the best stock truck yet, and says 2004 is a big step up from 2001 for noise and comfort. The 2006 Alpha is 'an order of magnitude better' on and off road. Autotrader calls it the ultimate H1, and Hagerty found Alphas worth over 40% more than a comparable 2004. The 1992–93 6.2 trucks are simple and a favorite of hard-core off-roaders, but slow.

faq.q: Should I worry about the 'No. 8 cylinder' crack?
faq.a: On turbo diesels from 1996 to early 1999, yes. One large Hummer dealer told Flash Off-Road that most cracks appear on '96 through early-'99 trucks, with '97s and '98s most common. GM changed the block casting from casting number C-159 (March 15, 1999); AM General started using the new blocks at E-019 (May 1, 1999). An 'F' in the fourth VIN digit means an AM General-built engine, which isn't at risk. Many at-risk engines were replaced under warranty.

The turbo diesel. Flash Off-Road owned all three. His 1995 gas truck could barely hold 40 mph over Loveland Pass, while his 1996 turbo diesel held 55 and returned about 11.5 mpg in town and 15 on the road. The gas and non-turbo diesel trucks run out of power at altitude. The gas truck also fords only 24 inches, versus 30 for the diesel, because the diesel's starter is waterproof and it has no ignition to drown.

faq.q: What does CTIS do, and do I need it?
faq.a: The central tire inflation system lets you inflate or deflate the tires from the cab, front and rear pairs together, through seals in the geared hubs. Airing down gives more grip in sand and rock. It was optional on some years (it's on the 1999 options list). Flash Off-Road says retrofitting it is hard and rarely economical, so buy a truck that has it if you want it.

Through 1998, H1s use Torsen I differentials, which owners can coax into locking with brake-throttle modulation. When ABS became mandatory in 1999, AM General moved to Torsen II with electronic TorqTrac4 traction control, which Flash Off-Road says is good in snow and loose dirt but weaker for rock crawling. The 2002 trucks got a higher torque-bias ratio. From 2003 a rear Eaton electric locker was offered, and front and rear lockers came with the 2004 and 2006 Off-Road Adventure package.

Flash Off-Road says not to run it past about 2,400 rpm, which is around 65 mph, if you want it to last. Faster driving burns the transfer case oil and strains a truck designed for unimproved roads. Below 65 he saw 13 to 15 mpg from a turbo diesel. A 1999 turbo diesel took 18 seconds to reach 60 mph according to the brochure; the Alpha took 13.5 according to Edmunds.
The 1999 brochure gives a maximum towed load of 7,710 lb for a turbo-diesel wagon and 8,050 lb for an open top. Edmunds says a properly equipped 2006 Alpha open top can tow 9,300 lb.

faq.q: Can I run aftermarket or H2 wheels?
faq.a: H1 wheels use an 8x6.5-inch bolt pattern with a 7-inch backset. Flash Off-Road says only AM General and GT/Cepek wheels have the correct offset and load rating for a truck that weighs 7,000 to 8,000 lb. Owners on Hummer4x4Offroad report that H2 wheels fit with modification, and Moab tour operators have run them. Non-factory wheels also need custom CTIS lines.

30 inches for a diesel, according to the 1999 brochure and Wikipedia, and 24 inches for the 1995–96 gas trucks. The geared hubs and transfer case vent to the air cleaner, so check that the vent lines and intake seals are intact before deep water.

faq.q: Is the Alpha just a re-engined H1?
faq.a: No. AM General told Flash Off-Road that the control arms were the only parts under the truck carried over from 2004. The Alpha has the 12,100-lb GVW upgrade's bigger brakes, halfshafts and springs, a new Sheppard steering box, helical-gear hubs, a longer front driveshaft and reshaped 51-gallon fuel tanks. The downside is that most of those parts are unique to one model year.

mods.why: Flash Off-Road reports owners clearing 39.5-inch tires with a 2-inch body lift. Predator's combined 2-inch suspension and 2-inch body lift is meant for tires up to 42 inches. Body lifts need block-off bars to hide the gap at the rear.
